extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, marketers, product managers, and founders creating product launch press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to guidance for writing and pitching a press release announcing a new product, including required format elements, journalist targeting, headline/copy guidance, visuals, and use of AI/tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard press release format
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the basic, expected elements so journalists can quickly parse the story: Headline; Lead; Dateline; Body; Company details (boilerplate); Media contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard structure so journalists recognise the release as news-ready. The template should include all these elements; templates and press release software can help ensure the correct format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline (also email subject line)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attention-grabbing headline about your product that mentions your main points and product’s USP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend extra time crafting the headline/subject line. Make it exciting, mention unique benefits or features, and consider adding numbers (they improve open rates). Avoid generic or bland titles like '[Company] Launches New Product'. If readers ask 'So what?' you need a better headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief overview of the story that answers: Who? What? When? Why? With what effect?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should succinctly communicate the newsworthiness. Use it to summarise the most important facts so a journalist can immediately grasp the story angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: A dateline to confirm you’re providing the most up-to-date information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include city and date as appropriate so recipients know timing and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body / story development
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation and expansion of the lead; the first paragraph should include the most newsworthy information and finish with secondary details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the body so the most important info is up front, then provide supporting details, quotes, specs or context. Keep paragraphs concise and journalist-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company details / boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: A short paragraph including company name, spokespeople, background information on the company and its products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear boilerplate to help journalists quickly understand the business and write about it; include succinct contextual details that explain the company’s position in market/category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: The author's or company’s/agency’s contact information included in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a specific contact (name, role, email, phone) so journalists can follow up for more information or interview opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and target relevant journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch to the journalists and bloggers who cover your type of product and can bring it to the spotlight rather than sending to everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a media contacts database and filters (location, topic/industry) or keyword search to identify reporters who wrote about similar products. This targeted approach is more effective than 'spray and pray'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine media list and research interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that the journalists you found are actually interested in the specific subtopic (e.g., natural and organic products vs. general cosmetics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do deeper research into writers’ recent coverage to ensure fit. Narrowing by specific beats or interests improves pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize outreach & establish a human connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send your press release to everybody—personalize your outreach and establish a human connection with journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the pitch to the journalist’s beat, reference relevant past coverage when appropriate, and follow up instead of relying on a single blanket message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up
rubrics_metrics.description: Following up after the initial pitch to increase chances of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send timely, polite follow-ups rather than assuming one email is enough; follow-up is part of targeted outreach and relationship-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on unique features and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize what makes your product stand out by highlighting unique features and benefits relevant to the target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to emphasize technical features (better for B2B/technical audiences) or customer benefits (better for consumer audiences). Use objective comparisons to competitors when useful. The guide suggests specific questions to answer: Why is it worth writing about? What are its unique features? How will it contribute to consumers’ lives? What makes it different? Can you compare it to competitor products? Does it come in varieties/sizes? Is there a formal launch event?

rubrics_metrics.name: Target a specific audience and their media
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the specific group(s) who will benefit most from your product and the news outlets/articles they read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select target audience from predefined options (industry players, customers, local communities) or define your own; tailor messaging and outlets to that audience so the story resonates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use high-quality visuals (photos, videos, GIFs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add images and videos to make your product announcement stand out, but avoid sending large attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed media directly into the release or host it via press release software or your brand newsroom; share the release via a link so journalists can access high-res assets without inbox clutter. Use press release platforms to include photos, videos, call-to-action buttons, and social media threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid large attachments; share accessible links
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send large files as attachments that can clutter journalists' inboxes and make emails harder to open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed media or host assets on a newsroom/asset link and include the link in the press release so recipients can download or preview as needed; linking also enables tracking opens/clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates and press release software
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage templates to ensure you include all important elements and use software to create visually rich releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates speed up production and reduce format errors; PR software can help embed media, suggest journalists, and distribute releases directly from the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI to draft and refine press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-powered tools can generate high-quality press release drafts, provide editing suggestions, and recommend journalists to pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a stepwise AI workflow: enter basic details (type, target audience, language), provide key messages (Problem Solved; Unique Value Proposition; Target Audience and Benefits), answer follow-up questions (AI will ask tailored questions), customize and edit the draft (adjust fonts, length, and copy), and use the AI Assistant's suggested improvements (the guide notes an AI review based on 11 key criteria). Finally, get contact recommendations based on keywords in the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customize length, style and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust header font styles and press release length to suit the outlet and presentation format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tune the content like a regular editor: shorten or expand as needed, ensure clarity and readability, and match stylistic conventions of your target media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include clear key messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and communicate the primary messages the press release should deliver (problem solved, UVP, target audience benefits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as specific as possible when stating these messages to reduce follow-up questions from journalists and to make the angle clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and measure engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use links and platform features to track opens and clicks on your press release distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding media and distributing via a newsroom or PR tool allows tracking; use this data to inform follow-ups and measure PR success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples and adapt proven formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult example press releases (feature launch, book launch, product line, cosmetics, food product) to see how different product announcements are structured and styled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples as inspiration for tone, structure, and media use, adapting the format to your product and audience rather than copying verbatim.
